title: stabilize-schema-v2-beta-headers-and-backcompat-shim-for-openai-compat
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: As we iterate on the API request/response schema to support richer structured output, more robust streaming, and clearer function/tool-calling semantics, we need a path for clients that expect the historical OpenAI-like request shape. This PR introduces a v2 schema (v2-beta) opt-in header, a backwards-compatible shim that maps legacy shapes to the new internal model, and several streaming stability fixes required by the new envelope format.

What this PR does: Adds an opt-in header X-Redwood-Schema: v2-beta. When present the gateway accepts and validates the v2 schema (stronger typing for "responses.tools" and top-level "structured_output"). When absent, the gateway continues to accept v1-shaped requests but runs a compatibility transformation to the v2 internal representation. The shim handles: 1) mapping legacy top-level "model" -> new "engine" + variant metadata; 2) mapping OpenAI-style "functions" to our internal "tools" schema; 3) legacy stop/temperature tokens normalization; 4) streaming envelope translation for clients that expect "data: {choices:...}" frames.

Streaming stability fixes: Adds sequence-numbered stream frames (stream_id + seq_no) so clients and servers can resume partial streams without re-decoding full sequences. Implements idempotent re-send handling on the runtime side (dedupe by stream_id+seq_no) and improves chunk assembly to avoid token splitting on UTF-8 boundaries. Also includes a reconnect/retry guide in docs and a new metric (stream.resume.rate) and alert (SLO: stream.resume > 99.9% over 10m).

Function/tool calling and structured output: The v2 schema formalizes tool outputs as typed objects with explicit schemas; we add strict validation (by default in v2-beta) but expose a permissive mode via header X-Redwood-Allow-Loose-Tools. For OpenAI-compat users we provide an intermediate translation layer that preserves the classic "function_call" field and maps to our ToolRun events while keeping determinism for reruns.

Backcompat & deprecation: This shim is intentionally conservative; no existing v1 clients should break. We will run the shim for all requests for 90 days, log usage by client version (user-agent + api-client header), and ship a deprecation announcement after 120 days. The v1 validation path will be deprecated at 180 days (with opt-out grace via feature flag). Detailed migration steps are included below.

Tests & CI: Unit tests for schema mapping, integration tests for streaming resume behavior, and a local canary e2e that exercises a real OpenAI-compat client were added. CI shows all checks passing; canary ran successfully against a small internal workload.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging with header opt-in only; 2) Enable shim globally behind runtime feature flag and run telemetry; 3) Promote header to beta and publish migration docs; 4) Monitor stream.resume.rate and model-fallback rates for 72-hour windows before wider rollout.

Checklist: - [x] Add v2 schema validation and header parsing - [x] Implement v1 -> v2 mapping shim - [x] Add streaming seq_no and dedupe logic - [x] Add integration tests and canary harness - [x] Update SDK compatibility layer tests - [x] Update docs and migration guide

Notes for reviewers: The change touches the gateway and the compatibility layer in runtime. I kept the transformation logic isolated under gateway/compat and added flags to control permissive behaviour. The most opinionated bits are the strict tool schema validation and the exact deprecation timeline; I'm open to pushing timelines if we want longer client notice.

Migration summary for customers: To opt into v2-beta immediately include the header: X-Redwood-Schema: v2-beta. To continue using older OpenAI shapes nothing is required for now; plan migration to v2-style tool outputs over the next 3 months. See release notes below for curl examples and SDK changes.

Streaming frames now include stream_id + seq_no for resumability and deduping. New metrics: stream.resume.rate and compat.mapping.errors. Migration guide added under docs/migration/v2-schema.md.
